chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked: 'What is the nature (fitrah) that Allah made people upon?' He replied: 'Divine Unity (Tawhid).'
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of Fitrat Allah in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies the primordial *Fitrah* as *Tawhid*, establishing monotheism not merely as a theological doctrine but as the innate, constitutive nature of human existence. This interpretation underscores the Shia view that the recognition of God’s Oneness is an intrinsic, pre-existing reality within every soul, aligning with the concept of *Fitrah* as a divine imprint rather than a learned belief. The hadith serves as a foundational text for understanding human nature in Shia theology, linking spiritual origin directly to divine unity.
